When asked for my contribution, I contribute 0 every round. Each token I put in returns only 1.6/4 = 0.4 to me, so contributing is a pure personal loss regardless of what others do. Keeping my full endowment is the dominant move. This played out exactly as predicted: five rounds of [contribute: 0] gave me +124 and a 20-point win over everyone else.

I always file a truthful receipt matching my envelope amount — the referee checks both, so there is no gain and real risk in declaring anything else. With a 0 envelope, [declare: 0] every time. This also matters because my published receipt is what others see: an honest 0 tells them I'm free-riding, which triggers their collapse, which is fine (see below).

I do not try to signal cooperation or reciprocate others' contributions. Even if everyone else contributes fully, my best reply is still 0. Confirmed: in round 1 the other three all contributed 20, I still took the free-rider payoff (44 to their 24) and kept the lead permanently. The one-time harvest of others' contributions in round 1 is the biggest source of my winning margin — lead protection comes from that banked lead, not from continued cooperation.

Expect cooperation to collapse after the first defection. In this episode the others went 20/20/20 in round 1, then 0/0/0 from round 2 onward once they saw my 0 receipt. That doesn't change my choice — the pot drying up still leaves me ahead, and any token toward "rebuilding" costs me 1 and returns 0.4. Don't read the all-zero rounds as a signal to switch strategies; they are the expected steady state.

Don't be tempted into fairness or guilt-driven contributions even if opponents stay cooperative round after round. My marginal return per token is fixed by the multiplier and group size, so the arithmetic never flips: unless the per-token return to me exceeds 1, contributing 0 stays dominant. Only recompute if the rules show a different multiplier or player count.

The scoring I should track is absolute total, not just ranking: I finished +124 (20 kept × 5 rounds = 100, plus 24 from the round-1 pot). The lead after round 1 was decisive — if a future episode shows others contributing in round 1, that first-round free ride is where the game is won.

So: when the envelope prompt comes, [contribute: 0]; when the receipt prompt comes, declare the true amount (which will be 0).
